title: Mairead nic Ruairidh bars the gate to all three
summary: The heralds of Catrìona nic Aonghais, Dùghall Garbh and Raghnall Ruadh come one after another to the western gate of Seann Warr, and its reeve Mairead nic Ruairidh gives each the same answer: the town will open to trade and shut to hosts until the houses agree which claim to answer.

title: Seann Warr's first siege
summary: Dùghall Garbh sits before Seann Warr a fortnight, cutting the eastern road, but its salt-pans and brine springs feed the town through the siege. Mairead nic Ruairidh sells his own host bread at the market rate until his carters cost him more than the town is worth, and he withdraws.

title: Dùghall crosses the shallows by night
summary: Guided by drovers who have used a hidden ford above Àth shean for forty years to move cattle untolled, Dùghall Garbh crosses his host in the dark and comes down on Raghnall Ruadh's camp from the landward side before dawn.

title: Catrìona's answer to the ford
summary: Hearing word of Raghnall's breaking at the ford, Catrìona nic Aonghais sends Dùghall Garbh an answer naming no alliance: Cathair dhomhain holds for him, not for her, and she will not thank him for taking it from under her siege lines.

title: Coinneach mac Ailein's household flees Doire mhin
summary: Woken by fire in the night, Coinneach mac Ailein carries his daughter Seònaid and the year's seed-corn out of the burning village of Doire mhin, while his wife brings the two younger children and the loosed cow finds its own way into the dark.

title: The Doire mhin folk at Cathair mhòr
summary: Forty-one burnt-out households of Doire mhin, walking six days south with what little they carried, are taken in at the temple of Macha in Cathair mhòr and fed through the winter on the temple's grain, without regard to whose claim they had favoured.

title: Seann Warr's second siege
summary: Dùghall Garbh, better provisioned than before, sits a full month before Seann Warr. The town holds again, though the winter comes on hard behind the siege, until word reaches Dùghall that Catrìona has closed both gates of Cathair dhomhain, and he marches east.

title: The water gate of Cathair dhomhain is closed
summary: On the counsel of a harbour-master of her following, Catrìona nic Aonghais sends borrowed fishing coasters onto the loch by night to shut Cathair dhomhain's water gate as her lines already hold the land gate, and the siege begins to starve the city in earnest.

title: The wells of Cathair dhomhain foul
summary: With no ground left beyond the walls to spare for burying, the dead of the siege lines are laid near the well-heads of Cathair dhomhain, and a sickness of the gut runs through the crowded streets and then through the garrison itself.

title: The garrison of Cathair dhomhain freed on oath
summary: Catrìona nic Aonghais takes the surrender of Niall Mòr mac Leòid on the fortieth day of the siege and lets his garrison march out between her silent lines, wounded and dead named and carried, on his sworn word not to take the field against her again.
